commit_subject: TcpStack tests: the memory admission gate - at the limit a SYN draws nothing, no connection and no RST, and the peer's retransmitted SYN is served once the footprint recedes; the test swaps the process-wide memory reader, so it runs alone (the TcpStack review's leftover)

TcpStack: the review's leaves recorded where they govern - a closed stream's unread bytes, one segment per partial ACK, RFC 5961's lower ack bound, the second lock of a data segment, no SND.WL1/WL2 check, IPv4 fragments, Dispose's order, the two components as classes, the test host's pool floor (the TcpStack review's leftovers)

Tests: TestBase without null-forgiving initializers - the helper is a nullable field behind a property that fails loud before TestInitialize, and TestContext is required (the TcpStack review's leftover)

Packets: a TCP, UDP or ICMP layer built into an IP packet clears its header only, where it cleared its payload too, which the IP packet's constructor had just cleared: a built packet's payload is zeroed once before it is copied in, not twice (the TcpStack review's leftover)

TcpStack: only an ACK that frees room or widens the window wakes a writer parked on a full window, where every acceptable segment did - a thread-pool hop and a semaphore node for each of the peer's own data segments, which free nothing (the TcpStack review's leftover)

TcpStack: a handshake given up logs a Debug line, one a second per stack like the admission gate's, where it left none - a kernel answers a SYN-ACK at once, so a give-up means the path to it is broken or the SYN was crafted; a test checks the line (the TcpStack review's leftover)

TcpStack tests: the packet, accept and wait helpers live once, in TcpTestHarness, where the three test files kept their own copies, diverged in optional parameters only; the files read it through using static, so no call changes (the TcpStack review's leftover)

TcpStack: PipeResumeWriterThreshold is gone with its check, which refused a 1-byte window - the stack enforces the advertised window before it writes, so the pipe's writer never paused and never resumed; the resume threshold is the pause threshold (the pipe's own 32 KB default is refused above a small window's pause threshold); a test takes the window's whole range (the TcpStack review's leftover)
TcpStack: the segment path tests TcpFlags by bit, where Enum.HasFlag boxed in the JIT's first-tier code, an allocation per test per segment until the method tiered up (the TcpStack review's leftover)
